what_this_is: which grocery each published answer was measured to. The plane names the destination NODE and the side table carries every place on it, because a node is not a shop and the cost model routed to the node
the_presentation_rule: the owner's decision, 2026-11-13: THE NODE PLUS THE SET, and the card chooses. The set is the truthful answer rather than a convenience -- the selection is a cost-argmin over NODES, so which of the places on the chosen node a household walks to is not something this pipeline computed and the artifact must not assert it

cells.why_this_number_sets_the_plane_width: 432 distinct destinations are named by at least one cell. A dense ordinal over those fits a uint8 plane only if it is at most 254; scripts/price_destination_encodings.py prices the options on the real plane rather than assuming

the_set_a_household_would_be_shown.what_ambiguous_means_here: the cell's journey ends at a node carrying more than one grocery, so the artifact names a SET and not a shop. That is the honest state of the computation, not a defect to be resolved by picking one

ties.what_this_is: whether the destination a household would be SHOWN is a property of the published answer or of the traversal order
ties.the_control_that_makes_a_zero_meaningful: scripts/measure_tie_flag.py holds the four-node construction and its positive control. The instrument is the same permutation; this reuses it on the destination rather than the flag
ties.what_it_means: exact bit-level cost ties between different destinations do not occur on this graph, so the destination is well defined here. It is latent, not absent -- quantising the cost would manufacture ties, and then the NAME shown would depend on heap order
